documents.content:
1. SYSTEM OVERVIEW AND ARCHITECTURE
UniCampus ERP serves as the enterprise transactional backbone managing the complete student academic and administrative lifecycle at Demo University. Deployed across the university primary data center with automated cloud failover, the platform integrates student bio-data records, semester course registration engines, institutional fee ledger links, digital bonafide certificate generation, and automated graduation degree audit trackers.

2. ACCESS PORTAL AND AUTHENTICATION
2.1 Portal Uniform Resource Locator: Students access the student portal via authenticated intranet and secure web links at https://erp.demo.edu.internal/student. Staff and faculty access administrative consoles at https://erp.demo.edu.internal/faculty-admin.
2.2 Single Sign-On Credentials: User authentication requires active institutional single-sign-on (SSO) credentials issued during initial enrollment by the Identity & Access Management Desk.

3. CORE FUNCTIONAL MODULES
3.1 Course Enrollment Engine: Operates during the notified Date of Registration (DOR) and Add/Drop windows. Displays core program courses, verifies prerequisite completions, validates credit limits (20 to 24 credits standard, overload up to 28 credits), and routes provisional baskets to Faculty Advisors for digital endorsement.
3.2 Fee Ledger Link: Synchronizes student financial accounts with PayVarsity. Reflects real-time fee demands, scholarship credit ledger postings, and automated clearance statuses.
3.3 Bonafide Certificate Generator: Enables self-service requests for authenticated study certificates, education loan fee structures, and passport transit endorsements featuring dynamic verification QR codes.
3.4 Degree Audit Tracker: Continuously evaluates completed curriculum credits against statutory degree requirements (e.g., 160 credits for B.Tech), highlighting outstanding core, elective, or non-credit requirements.

4. TROUBLESHOOTING FINANCIAL HOLDS AND SYSTEM INCIDENTS
4.1 Financial Hold Resolution: An account flagged with 'FINANCIAL-HOLD' blocks course enrollment and examination hall ticket downloads. Students must identify the originating department ledger on PayVarsity (Tuition, Hostel Mess, or Library fine) and complete remittance. System clearance syncs within two hours.
4.2 Credential Failures: Account lockouts resulting from five consecutive invalid password attempts require self-service password reset (SSPR) or logging a ticket on ResolveDesk under 'IT Services > ERP Account Support'.

documents.content:
1. SYSTEM MANDATE AND SCOPE
LearnSphere LMS constitutes Demo University's cloud-hosted academic learning management platform. Maintained by IT Services, LearnSphere provides digital pedagogical extensions for all credit-bearing lecture and laboratory courses, hosting course syllabi, lecture slides, assignment dropboxes, auto-graded coding environments, continuous assessment quizzes, and academic discussion forums.

2. ACCESS ENDPOINTS AND DASHBOARD SYNCHRONIZATION
2.1 Web Endpoints: Accessible to matriculated scholars at https://learn.demo.edu.internal and faculty instructors at https://learn.demo.edu.internal/instructor.
2.2 Roster Synchronization: Enrolled course rosters synchronize automatically from UniCampus ERP overnight following Faculty Advisor registration approvals. Courses registered during Add/Drop reflect within 24 hours of approval.

3. STUDENT SUBMISSION AND PARTICIPATION MODULES
3.1 Assignment Dropboxes: Supports student document submissions subject to strict format constraints (PDF, DOCX, ZIP). Submissions are time-stamped upon receipt. Upload attempts beyond announced deadlines are locked unless instructor late-submission windows are active.
3.2 Automated Coding Sandbox: Provides containerized execution sandboxes for engineering programming courses (DSA, OOP Java, Systems Programming), executing student code against test suites.
3.3 Internal Assessment Quiz Engine: Houses continuous internal assessment quizzes contributing toward Continuous Internal Evaluation (CIE) ledgers.
3.4 Discussion Boards: Secure interactive academic message threads between students, instructors, and graduate Teaching Assistants.

4. TROUBLESHOOTING AND TECHNICAL SUPPORT
4.1 Upload Failures: If a file submission fails, users must verify that file sizes remain within the 25 MB per-file threshold and that network timeouts are not occurring. If errors persist, students should capture error screenshots and submit an incident ticket via ResolveDesk under 'LMS Technical Support'.
4.2 Missing Course Shells: If an officially enrolled course fails to populate on the LearnSphere dashboard 24 hours after ERP registration, the student must log a ResolveDesk ticket attaching their ERP course registration receipt.

The platform maintains air-gapped database mirrors during active testing and manages confidential assessment workflows.

2.2 Single Sign-On Linkage: Authentication relies on unified enterprise student credentials synchronized with the Identity & Access Management directory.

documents.title: ResolveDesk Ticketing User Guide: SLA Tiers and Ticket Escalation
retrieval_signals: how to report IT problem Demo University
documents.content:
1. PLATFORM ARCHITECTURE AND FUNCTION
ResolveDesk functions as Demo University's centralized enterprise service management and omnichannel ticketing platform. Hosted within the private campus cloud, it routes technical IT incidents, classroom AV maintenance, facilities work orders, On-Duty pre-approvals, and formal student grievances to appropriate administrative units under strict statutory Service Level Agreements (SLAs).

2. ACCESS AND CASE LOGGING WORKFLOW
2.1 Portal Endpoint: Accessible via web and mobile interfaces at https://resolve.demo.edu.internal using university SSO credentials. Support staff access agent dashboards at https://resolve.demo.edu.internal/agent.
2.2 Categorization Framework: Users select specialized queues:
  - IT Services & Campus Networks (Wi-Fi, ERP, LMS, Lab PCs, biometrics).
  - Campus Operations & Facilities (classroom electrical, air conditioning, plumbing).
  - Academic Grievances & Attendance (sessional marks, grading, condonation).
  - Student Affairs & Welfare (OD leave requests, club sanctions, hostel complaints).
2.3 Docket Details and Attachments: Users specify affected assets (e.g., room number, terminal IP, transaction ID) and may attach diagnostic screenshots, logs, or documentation up to 10 MB (PDF, PNG, JPEG).

3. SLA TIERS AND ESCALATION TIMELINES
3.1 Standard SLA Framework:
  - Tier 1 (Technical & Facilities Incidents): Target response within 24 hours; resolution within 48 to 72 hours.
  - Tier 2 (Department Grievance - Level 1): Statutory resolution within 5 working days.
  - Tier 3 (Central Grievance Committee - Level 2): Hearing and determination within 10 working days.
  - Tier 4 (University Ombudsman - Level 3): Binding determination within 20 working days.
3.2 Escalation Mechanism: If an assigned ticket breaches its resolution timeline or produces an unsatisfactory outcome, users may activate the 'Escalate' button within 48 hours to route the case to higher governance tiers.

documents.content:
1. INFRASTRUCTURE OVERVIEW
Demo University operates a high-density enterprise wireless network covering all academic blocks (Newton Hall, Turing Complex, Ramanujan Block, Aryabhata Wing, Faraday Tower), Valmiki Central Library, Student Activity Centre, and the East Residential Enclave (Cauvery, Nilgiri, Vindhya, Brahmaputra, Sarojini, Gargi). The network utilizes 802.1X authentication over WPA2/WPA3-Enterprise standards.

2. NETWORK IDENTIFIERS (SSIDS)
2.1 DemoUniv-Secure: Primary secured network for registered students, faculty, and administrative personnel, delivering encrypted access across academic and residential zones.
2.2 DemoUniv-Guest: Bandwidth-throttled captive-portal network for official visitors, requiring temporary mobile OTP authorization provisioned via CampusPass.

3. DEVICE CONFIGURATION PARAMETERS (802.1X)
To connect a personal computing device (laptop, smartphone, or tablet) to DemoUniv-Secure, users must configure the following standard network settings:
  a) EAP Method: PEAP (Protected Extensible Authentication Protocol).
  b) Phase 2 Inner Authentication: MSCHAPv2.
  c) CA Certificate: Select 'Use system certificates' (Domain: demo.edu.internal) or select 'Do not validate' if prompted by legacy operating systems.
  d) Identity: Enter full university enrollment number / student ID (e.g., `2024BCSE101`).
  e) Anonymous Identity: Leave blank.
  f) Password: Enter institutional single-sign-on (SSO) password.

4. DEVICE LIMITS AND TROUBLESHOOTING
4.1 Permitted Concurrency: Each matriculated student is permitted a maximum of two concurrently active MAC addresses registered on the RADIUS network directory.
4.2 Troubleshooting IP and Lease Issues: If a device fails to acquire a DHCP lease, the user should forget the network profile, restart wireless radios, and reconnect. Persistent authentication failures or localized access point outages must be reported on ResolveDesk under 'Network & Wi-Fi Issues' specifying device MAC address and building room number.

IT code of conduct Demo University
documents.content:
1. PURPOSE AND POLICY MANDATE
This policy establishes mandatory operational guidelines, ethical standards, and legal compliance obligations governing the utilization of Demo University computing hardware, campus enterprise networks, wireless communications, enterprise software platforms, and digital identities.

2. AUTHORIZED ACCESS AND CREDENTIAL INTEGRITY
2.1 Personal and Non-Transferable Access: University computing accounts, LMS access credentials, and network access logins are strictly personal to the individual to whom they are provisioned. Sharing passwords or multi-factor authentication codes with peers, relatives, or external third parties is strictly prohibited.
2.2 Individual Accountability: Account owners are held legally and administratively accountable for all network traffic, file transactions, and system requests originating under their provisioned credentials.

3. EXPLICITLY PROHIBITED COMPUTING ACTIVITIES
Users connecting to university computing assets or network backbones are strictly forbidden from engaging in:
  a) Network Reconnaissance and Intrusion: Port scanning, vulnerability probing, packet sniffing, packet injection, or running automated credential-stuffing scripts against internal or external subnets.
  b) Copyright Infringement & Peer-to-Peer Transfers: Utilizing torrent clients, running unauthorized file-sharing hubs, or downloading copyrighted media, pirated textbooks, or unlicensed commercial software.
  c) Unauthorized Resource Consumption: Deploying cryptocurrency mining software, hosting unauthorized public web servers, or running automated bots that degrade shared bandwidth.
  d) Malicious Code Dissemination: Developing, propagating, or hosting malware, worms, trojans, ransomware, or phishing landing pages.

4. ENFORCEMENT, SURVEILLANCE, AND DISCIPLINARY SANCTIONS
4.1 Automated Network Isolation: The Network Operations Centre (NOC) employs automated intrusion detection systems. Detected severe policy violations trigger instantaneous MAC and account isolation.
4.2 Disciplinary Actions: Violations of this policy incur immediate account revocation and referral to the Proctorial Board under POL-DISCIPLINE, resulting in fines, academic suspension, or expulsion.

documents.title: Password Lifecycle, Multi-Factor Authentication, and Account Reset Policy
retrieval_signals: Identity and Access Management desk location

OTP not coming for password reset
documents.content:
1. PURPOSE AND SECURITY PRINCIPLES
This policy defines the standards governing user identity provisioning, password complexity, account lockout thresholds, multi-factor authentication (MFA) requirements, and verified account reset workflows across Demo University enterprise systems.

2. PASSWORD COMPLEXITY AND LIFECYCLE RULES
2.1 Complexity Standards: User passwords across UniCampus ERP, LearnSphere LMS, and network access accounts must possess:
  a) Minimum length of 10 alphanumeric characters.
  b) At least one uppercase letter, one lowercase letter, one numeric digit, and one special symbol.
  c) Prohibition of easily guessable tokens, sequential numbers, or personal biographic elements (birthdates, student registration numbers).
2.2 Lifecycle and Rotation: Passwords remain valid for 180 calendar days. Automated reminder notifications are dispatched via institutional email at 14, 7, and 1 day prior to expiration.

3. ACCOUNT LOCKOUT AND DEFENSE THRESHOLDS
To mitigate brute-force credential guessing, user accounts are automatically locked upon five consecutive failed authentication attempts. Locked accounts remain suspended for a mandatory lockout window of 30 minutes before automatic retry is permitted.

4. SELF-SERVICE AND PHYSICAL ACCOUNT RESET PROCEDURES
4.1 Self-Service Password Reset (SSPR): Users who have registered an authenticated recovery mobile phone number or secondary email may initiate automated SSPR via the login portal, receiving a time-limited 6-digit OTP verification code.
4.2 In-Person Identity Verification: Students unable to resolve account lockouts via SSPR must visit the Identity & Access Management Desk, located in Turing Complex, Ground Floor Basement Server Hub. Re-credentialing requires physical presentation of their official Demo University RFID Smart ID card.
4.3 Remote Verification via ResolveDesk: Outstation students or scholars engaged in verified internships may log an account recovery ticket on ResolveDesk, attaching certified government photo identification to verify identity before credentials are regenerated.

documents.content:
1. PURPOSE AND INSTITUTIONAL SCOPE
This policy establishes security controls, perimeter firewall architectures, server virtualization provisioning norms, and network hygiene requirements protecting university digital infrastructure against cyber intrusions, external vulnerabilities, and unauthorized access.

2. PERIMETER FIREWALL RULES AND TRAFFIC FILTERING
2.1 Outbound & Inbound Controls: The university core firewall operates default-deny postures on non-standard incoming ports. Standard web protocols (HTTP/HTTPS) and verified academic traffic are permitted.
2.2 Development Port Restrictions: Direct outbound access on development protocols (such as SSH on port 22, alternate HTTP on port 8080, database ports 3306/5432) from general student residential Wi-Fi subnets is restricted to prevent botnet propagation and unauthorized remote shells.

3. TECHNICAL RESEARCH & HACKATHON SERVER PROVISIONING (REL-022)
3.1 VM & GPU Provisioning: Student academic teams or chartered technical clubs organizing hackathons or conducting AI/cloud research may request dedicated virtual machines or GPU containers hosted on LabServer Forge.
3.2 Application and Whitelisting Procedure: The student lead submits a technical request on ResolveDesk at least five working days prior to project initiation, specifying required CPU/RAM configurations, targeted inbound/outbound ports (e.g., 8080, 22), and receiving endorsement from the Department HOD. Network Security Services (NSS) validates security isolation and deploys temporary firewall whitelisting rules.

4. PROHIBITED NETWORK HARDWARE
Connecting personal Wi-Fi routers, unmanaged network switches, wireless repeaters, or unauthorized DHCP servers to hostel LAN wall jacks or academic ethernet ports is strictly prohibited. Detected rogue devices are blacklisted immediately via port-security shutdown on core switches.

1. OPERATIONAL CHARTER AND MANDATE
Technical Assistants (TAs) are full-time technical staff members assigned across engineering and computing laboratories. Governed under IT Services and academic department oversight, this charter defines daily machine maintenance obligations, hardware health diagnostics, operating system image deployments, and escalation workflows.

2. DAILY PRE-SESSION WORKSTATION AUDITS
2.1 Morning Inspection: Prior to the commencement of morning academic laboratory sessions (08:30 AM), Technical Assistants must perform physical inspections of assigned lab bays:
  - Verifying power supply continuity and surge protector operations.
  - Auditing input peripherals (keyboards, optical mice) and display monitor cables.
  - Ensuring network patch cords are seated and verifying local subnet connectivity.
2.2 Operating System Image Integrity: Maintaining standardized dual-boot Linux and Windows workstation disk images, ensuring course software dependencies (compilers, IDEs, databases) remain uncorrupted.

3. MAINTENANCE, LOGGING, AND REPAIR WORKFLOWS
3.1 Minor Hardware Failures: TAs maintain emergency spares of keyboards, mice, network cables, and RAM modules. Defective peripherals are swapped immediately from lab stock.
3.2 Major Hardware Breakdowns: Component failures involving motherboards, power supply units (PSUs), or network switches are logged within four hours on ResolveDesk under 'Hardware Support'.
3.3 Equipment Safety & Calibration: Assisting faculty instructors with experimental test benches, ensuring adherence to electrical grounding standards, and supervising lab cleanliness.

4. COGNITIVE DISAMBIGUATION NOTICE
This charter applies exclusively to full-time technical staff (Technical Assistants - TAs). Academic tutoring, grading, and tutorial duties are executed by graduate Teaching Assistants (TAs) governed under ACAD-POL-007.

documents.title: Campus Network Operations Centre (NOC) Architecture and Escalations
retrieval_signals: Wi-Fi is down in Newton hall did NOC respond
fiber optic cable cut on campus
documents.content:
1. MISSION AND PHYSICAL INFRASTRUCTURE
The Network Operations Centre (NOC) operates from the Central Server Hub in the Turing Complex Ground Floor Basement. Acting as the nerve center for campus telecommunications and enterprise networking, the NOC manages core layer-3 routing switches, distribution fiber trunks, enterprise wireless controllers, and dual redundant tier-1 Internet Service Provider (ISP) gateway links.

2. CAMPUS BACKBONE TOPOLOGY
2.1 Optical Fiber Trunking: High-capacity multi-gigabit optical fiber rings interconnect the North Academic Quadrant, South Research Hub, Central Administration, and East Residential Enclave.
2.2 Redundant Core Routing: The core routing architecture employs automated failover protocol switching, ensuring uninterrupted network operations in the event of primary link or distribution switch failures.

3. INCIDENT MONITORING AND ESCALATION PROTOCOLS
3.1 24/7 Telemetry Monitoring: NOC monitoring consoles continuously poll distribution switches, access points, and server virtual machines. Link state down alerts trigger instantaneous technician dispatch.
3.2 Incident Severity Tiers:
  - Severity 1 (Campus-Wide Outage / Core Link Down): NOC Lead mobilizes emergency response within 15 minutes. Escalation to Director of IT Infrastructure within 30 minutes.
  - Severity 2 (Block-Level / Distribution Trunk Failure): On-site diagnosis within 45 minutes; restoration within 2 to 4 hours.
  - Severity 3 (Isolated Access Point / Floor Switch Failure): Resolution scheduled within standard working hours (SLA: 24 hours).

4. MAINTENANCE WINDOWS AND CAMPUS ADVISORIES
Scheduled firmware updates, core routing table revisions, and disruptive infrastructure upgrades are conducted exclusively during designated maintenance windows (Sundays between 01:00 AM and 05:00 AM). The NOC publishes advance maintenance advisories via institutional email at least 48 hours prior to scheduled disruptions.

1. REGULATORY PURPOSE
This operational manual defines user protocols, hardware security standards, and ethical operating rules for desktop personal computers (Lab PCs) installed across departmental computing suites and software studios in the Turing Complex, Faraday Tower, Newton Hall, and Ramanujan Block.

2. GENERAL OPERATING HYGIENE AND ENTRY RULES
2.1 Environmental Preservation: Eating meals, consuming snacks, or bringing open beverage containers into computer laboratories is strictly forbidden. Sealed water bottles must remain stored inside personal backpacks.
2.2 Identification Display: Students must visibly wear their official Demo University RFID Smart ID card while inside laboratory facilities and present credentials upon request by Technical Assistants.

3. COMPUTING INTEGRITY AND PERMITTED USE
3.1 Prohibition of Unauthorized Software: Students are strictly forbidden from downloading, executing, or installing personal software, gaming clients, cryptocurrency miners, or unlicensed executables onto Lab PCs. Workstations run standardized centralized images; local administrator privileges are not provisioned to students.
3.2 Peripheral Protection: Removing, disconnecting, or swapping system peripherals (monitors, keyboards, mice, power cords, HDMI cables) between workstations without permission from the Technical Assistant is prohibited.
3.3 Data Storage & Reboot Hygiene: Local hard drives are purged during automated nightly reboots. Students must store coursework and project files on institutional cloud storage or course repository accounts.

4. HARDWARE VANDALISM AND PUNITIVE MEASURES
Defacing computer casings, prying off keyboard keycaps, or intentionally damaging internal components constitutes property destruction under POL-DISCIPLINE. Infractions incur 100% replacement restitution billed via PayVarsity and referral to the Proctorial Board for disciplinary suspension.

1. MISSION AND MANDATE
Network Security Services (NSS) operates as the specialized cybersecurity and threat defense division within IT Services. Stationed within the Turing Complex Central Server Hub, NSS manages campus perimeter next-generation firewalls, intrusion prevention systems (IPS), web content filtering gateways, and secure virtual private network (VPN) tunnels.

2. CONTENT FILTERING AND PORT GOVERNANCE
2.1 Statutory Filtering Categories: The perimeter gateway blocks access to known malicious domains, phishing hosts, gambling portals, peer-to-peer torrent trackers, and explicit content networks in compliance with national cyber regulations.
2.2 Default Closed Port Architecture: To safeguard student devices against external network probes, non-standard outbound and inbound ports (including telnet, raw database listeners, and unencrypted file transfer ports) are closed by default across residential and general campus Wi-Fi subnets.

3. RESEARCH AND ACADEMIC WHITELISTING PROCEDURE
3.1 Legitimate Academic Exceptions: Faculty members, research scholars, and students conducting verified capstone projects who require access to blocked academic repositories, remote research instruments, or specialized development ports (such as SSH on port 22 or web services on port 8080) may request formal firewall whitelisting.
3.2 Application Workflow: The applicant submits an official 'Firewall Whitelisting Exception' ticket on ResolveDesk, attaching a project abstract endorsed by their Course Instructor or HOD. NSS reviews the technical specification, validates source/destination IP addresses, and implements policy exceptions within two working days.

4. DISAMBIGUATION NOTICE
This technical security standard applies to Network Security Services (NSS) within IT Services. The National Service Scheme (NSS) community volunteer organization operates independently under Clubs and Student Activities (DEPT-SAC).

3.1 Smart ID Authentication: Admittance requires physical swiping of the student's Demo University RFID Smart ID card at turnstiles linked to CampusPass. Workstation login requires active university SSO credentials.

documents.content:
1. PURPOSE AND WORKFLOW SCOPE
This Standard Operating Procedure defines the systematic diagnostic steps, audit verification protocols, and database rectification workflows required to resolve classroom IoT biometric edge terminal synchronization failures, RFID card-read errors, and AttendEdge attendance discrepancies.

2. TERMINAL HARDWARE ARCHITECTURE
Classroom attendance edge units located at lecture hall doors capture RFID card proximity taps and biometric scans, caching raw timestamp logs locally before synchronizing across campus networks to the central AttendEdge database.

3. DISCREPANCY RECTIFICATION WORKFLOW (REL-017)
When an edge terminal fails to synchronize attendance data (causing registered students to reflect as absent despite physical attendance), the following multi-department workflow is enforced:
3.1 Step 1 — Ticket Logging: Within 48 hours of the incident, the student logs an 'Attendance Biometric Glitch' ticket on ResolveDesk, specifying course code, date, lecture time slot, and classroom door number.
3.2 Step 2 — IT Telemetry & Raw Log Audit: An IT Services support technician extracts local diagnostic logs from the specific classroom IoT terminal, checking for hardware crash dumps, buffer overflow, or network timeout records to verify physical presence timestamps.
3.3 Step 3 — Faculty Physical Reconciliation: The Course Instructor cross-verifies manual classroom notes or signature rosters to corroborate physical classroom presence.
3.4 Step 4 — Academic Authorization: The Head of Department and Dean of Academic Affairs review the joint technical and faculty report, authorizing a retroactive database patch.
3.5 Step 5 — Database Patch & Sync: IT Services applies the authorized attendance adjustment in AttendEdge, updating cumulative attendance percentages within 24 hours.
